question: Does an established non-perturbative positive-transfer, correlation-decay, zero-free, or tensor-network method directly yield a controlled fair/intermediate L5 LER curve beyond p=.05?
scope: Primary-source and Local-Wiki method audit only; no sampling, fit, threshold, decoder run, or new contraction.
candidate_families: physical even-moment hierarchy of the logical twist ratio
acceptance: State the exact LER target and why a scalar partition-function approximation is or is not sufficient.
For every candidate, identify the theorem assumptions, the first failed interface condition, and whether a bounded feasibility test remains meaningful.
Use primary papers and separate established results from project-specific inference.
Select at most one smallest target-preserving feasibility test; do not authorize a production curve or a fit.
stop_rule: Stop if no existing theorem directly controls the public-record l1 norm. Preserve the unresolved analytic band and register only the cheapest diagnostic of the remaining target-preserving route.
decision: No reviewed scalar partition, correlation-decay, positive-polytope, or MPS theorem directly controls the LER public-record l1 norm under the hard charge constraints. The physical even-moment hierarchy is the only reviewed route that preserves the estimand; its smallest next test is a no-new-sampling moment-degree feasibility matrix.
